A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-REF research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original routing, rejection, calibration, latency, gradient-masking and transfer experiments, alongside MMLU case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds confidence-failure examples and a subject-area analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain correctness-based token annotation, unconfident-sample subsampling, gradient masking, confidence-score normalization and threshold-based routing/rejection. Expanding Self-REF's name and documenting alpha selection do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, OpenbookQA, GSM8K and MedQA, including rejection on MMLU/OpenbookQA and transfer from OpenbookQA to MMLU. The added subject-area analysis examines existing MMLU coverage.

E2.justification: The four confidence baselines remain Verbalizing Uncertainty, Verbalizing Yes/No Tokens, Zero-shot Logits and Fine-tuned Logits. Random routing already appears in v2 Figures 2, 4 and 5; v3's expanded caption does not add that comparator.

E3.justification: Table 3 revises the reported multiple-choice prompt for the logits baselines to explicitly require choosing one of A–D. This is a limited prompt refinement; model configurations, budgets, metrics and routing/rejection procedures remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v3 adds overconfidence and underconfidence case studies in Section 5.6/Figure 6, plus a subject-area breakdown across four correctness/confidence groups in Appendix E. These extend v2's favorable routing examples; the existing masking, calibration and transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose the same fixed inference seed, 2024, and deterministic decoding. Neither adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–5 retain their quantitative results. New Figure 6 reports a confidently incorrect computer-science answer and an unconfidently correct European-history answer; Appendix E newly lists the leading subject categories for each correctness/confidence group.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, augmented-dataset construction, subsampling expression, confidence-score formula and decision thresholds are retained. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims that lightweight confidence-token training improves downstream routing and rejection utility. The expanded name and future-work proposals do not change the claimed achieved contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of subject-specific confidence failures and clustered verbal-confidence scores. It removes v2's explicit privacy and data-leakage caveats from Section 6 and Appendix A, while retaining the limitation that network transmission costs are excluded.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.3 identifies MMLU validation-set evaluation and reports a GSM8K test count of 1,331. Appendix C.1 newly documents validation-based alpha selection using unconfident-to-confident ratios from 1:1 to 1:5. These are added disclosures; the existing hyperparameter and hardware tables are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including Chuang et al. (2025), Duan et al. (2024), R-tuning and the OpenbookQA source, and revises clinical-application citations. The positioning against external routers, consistency-based uncertainty and rejection-training methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits passages, expands Self-REF's name, changes author ordering, develops the conclusion and reorganizes appendix headings with new subsections. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout, extensively rescales and relocates displays, and revises captions and table headings. New Figure 6 combines a relocated catheter example with two new cases; the remaining earlier case studies appear in Figures 7–8.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's favorable routing examples, v3 makes confidence failures more assessable through Section 5.6 and Appendix E, while added split and sampling details improve reproducibility. These provide a limited net quality gain. The new analysis remains qualitative, and removing the specific privacy/data-leakage caveats weakens the discussion of deployment risks.
